`diag_open` shall write the invocation at the head of the companion, and shall leave the module inert where it is given no path — every later call then writing to standard error alone, so that no call site tests whether a companion exists.
A companion that cannot be opened shall be a diagnostic and a recorded failure rather than a fatal one: the user asked for a report and a debug file, and losing the second is no reason to withhold the first.

Every write to the companion shall be flushed before the call returns.
This is the property the companion exists for rather than an implementation detail. A run that faults, is killed, or exhausts memory is precisely the run worth diagnosing, and a log assembled in memory and written at exit is lost exactly then. The cost is a flush per diagnostic, which a run producing a diagnostic per file will not notice.

`diag_parse_failure` shall record one unparsable region as the file, the lines it spans, and the source text of those lines, read out of the mapping with an explicit length since the mapping is not NUL-terminated.
The text shall be bounded, and where it is truncated the number of lines omitted shall be stated. A file the grammar could follow nowhere would otherwise be copied into the log entire, which serves no reader and may disclose more of a private tree than whoever attached the log intended (HLR-195).

trace.name: Unparsable Source Recorded in the Debug Companion

llr.text: The companion shall carry a timestamp on each entry, and the report shall carry none. A log nobody watched being produced needs to say when each thing happened; a report must be byte-identical across two runs over one target (HLR-032). The companion is a record *of* a run rather than a result *of* one, which is the line the timestamps sit on.

test.name: the_sink_and_the_dispatcher_are_classified
test.purpose: A function many call and which calls nothing is a utility sink, a function lying on every shortest path and calling widest is a god object, and a function with one undirected neighbour is peripheral — the three classifications, over one hand-built graph.

test.name: an_ordinary_function_is_classified_as_nothing
test.purpose: Six of the nine functions are classified as nothing at all, which keeps the case above from passing against an implementation that classifies everything. `main` and `boot` are the sharpest: each passes the hub half of the utility-sink test and fails the authority half.

test.name: a_classification_names_the_metric_and_the_value
test.purpose: Each classification carries the measurement that triggered it and the value that measurement took, so a reader can trace it back to the graph rather than take it on trust.

test.name: a_rank_is_a_position_not_a_score
test.purpose: The top of a distribution ranks at 100 whatever the size of the graph, and the raw score it was reached from is nowhere near the threshold as a number — the property that lets one default serve graphs of any size.

test.name: a_god_object_outranks_a_utility_sink
test.purpose: With thresholds loose enough that one function satisfies both centrality tests, it is classified as a god object: masking its edges subsumes masking its incoming ones, and the more specific claim is the more useful one.

test.name: a_centrality_class_outranks_a_peripheral_one
test.purpose: With a core depth above every coreness in the graph, the two functions the centrality tests named keep their classes and everything else becomes peripheral — a function those tests spoke about is part of the connected centre by construction.

test.name: a_graph_with_no_nodes_classifies_nothing
test.purpose: An empty graph classifies nothing and is not a failure, as an analysis short of its inputs never is.

test.name: scores_within_the_tolerance_hold_one_position
test.purpose: Two scores differing in the last bits hold one position in the distribution, so an iterative computation cannot classify the same source differently on two machines.

test.name: scores_outside_the_tolerance_are_ordered
test.purpose: The tolerance is relative and floored at one, so a betweenness in the thousands and a HITS score in the millionths are each ordered correctly by the same comparison.

test.name: the_call_view_is_not_modified
test.purpose: The requirement the phase is built on, asserted directly: the vertex and edge counts of the graph every other analysis reads are the same after purification as before, and the view is a different object.

test.name: a_sink_keeps_its_outgoing_edges
test.purpose: Over a hand-built classification, a utility sink loses the edges into it and keeps the edges out of it — the asymmetry the fixture tree cannot show, because its sink calls nothing.

test.name: a_god_object_loses_both_directions
test.purpose: A god object loses its edges in both directions and stays in the view: it is masked rather than excluded, being part of the centre the layering is read from.

test.name: a_peripheral_node_is_excluded_rather_than_placed
test.purpose: A peripheral function is marked out of the view and holds no edge, so nothing downstream can give it a recovered layer.

test.name: the_view_keeps_the_graphs_own_node_identifiers
test.purpose: The view has the same vertex count as the graph, so an excluded node is marked rather than renumbered away and a vertex of the view indexes the node table directly.

test.name: the_view_counts_what_the_masking_removed
test.purpose: The retained edges plus the masked edges are all of the call edges, so a view cannot drop one without reporting it.

test.name: every_class_names_itself_and_the_action_it_took
test.purpose: One definition of each class name, metric name, and masking action, so four renderers and the saved record cannot disagree about what a classification is called or about what it did.

test.name: the_report_carries_one_row_per_classification
test.purpose: The report carries one row per classified function and none for the ordinary ones, each naming the metric, the value, and the action, beside the thresholds in force and the counts the view was left with.

test.name: the_report_rows_are_ordered_by_file_and_line
test.purpose: The rows are ordered by an explicit key before a renderer sees them, so no library enumeration order reaches the output.

test.name: an_edgeless_graph_scores_zero_and_classifies_no_centrality
test.purpose: A call view with no edges leaves every hub and authority score at zero and yields no utility sink and no god object, the decomposition being undefined there and not asked for.

test.name: functions_with_equal_scores_hold_one_position
test.purpose: Two functions of the same shape hold one position in every distribution and classify alike, whichever order the library enumerated them in — the observable half of an ordering made exact with the node identifier breaking ties and the tolerance applied over it afterwards.

test.name: a_manifest_statement_overrules_a_computed_class
test.purpose: A manifest statement returning the planted dispatcher to ordinary governs: the class is the manifest's, the row is marked as coming from it, and nothing the statement did not name changes.

test.name: a_manifest_may_keep_a_classified_function_in_the_view
test.purpose: A statement stating a class and withholding its masking action keeps the classification reportable and the function's edges in the recovery view — the correction a user makes when `elc` read the graph correctly and drew the wrong conclusion from it.

test.name: a_manifest_statement_naming_nothing_is_recorded_unmatched
test.purpose: A statement naming a function no analysed file defines is recorded as unmatched and the run continues, while a statement beside it still governs.

test.name: a_statement_naming_a_file_matches_only_that_file
test.purpose: Naming the file is precise in both directions: a statement about a same-named function in another file leaves this one alone, and is recorded as having matched nothing.

test.name: a_malformed_manifest_is_rejected_rather_than_partly_applied
test.purpose: A file that is not JSON is refused whole: the read fails and no statement is left behind for the caller to apply.

test.name: well_formed_json_that_is_not_a_manifest_is_rejected
test.purpose: Three files that parse as JSON and are not manifests — no version, no classifications array, a class name this build does not know — are each refused, which is the judgement Jansson does not make.

test.name: a_manifest_from_a_later_build_is_rejected
test.purpose: A manifest stamped with a version this build does not read is refused rather than half-understood.

test.name: a_written_manifest_reads_back
test.purpose: The round trip: every classification the run made is written, ordered by file and line, and read back by the same module without modification.

test.name: manifest_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Teardown tolerates a NULL and a zeroed record, which is what makes one unconditional release enough for every path through the run.

test.name: a_layered_graph_recovers_its_layers
test.purpose: Three directories in a plain layering fold into three layers in the order the calls run, over the vertices the view retained.

test.name: an_outlier_member_does_not_move_its_directory
test.purpose: A function called from the layer beneath its own sits last in the topological order; the directory holding it stays where the bulk of its edges point, which a fold reading the latest member would not.

test.name: an_excluded_function_is_given_no_layer
test.purpose: A directory all of whose functions the view excluded receives no layer at all rather than the bottom one.

test.name: nothing_surviving_purification_proposes_nothing
test.purpose: A recovery view retaining no function is an omission with its reason stated, not an empty proposal and not an error.

test.name: a_cyclic_view_reports_the_cycles_instead_of_an_order
test.purpose: A view holding a mutual pair is reported as its strongly connected component — as a membership, not as a chain of arrows — and no layering and no proposal are produced.

test.name: the_proposal_is_an_argument_list
test.purpose: The proposal is rendered as the `--stratum` and `--stratum-order` arguments that would declare it, patterns and order both quoted.

test.name: the_declarations_run_deepest_directory_first
test.purpose: Where one recovered directory is an ancestor of another, the descendant is declared first, so that an ancestor pattern cannot claim the descendant's files.

test.name: two_runs_over_one_graph_propose_one_layering
test.purpose: Two runs over one graph produce identical rows and an identical argument list, so neither the library's enumeration order nor the fold's arithmetic reaches the output.

test.name: the_proposal_reaches_the_report_and_nothing_else
test.purpose: The rows and the argument list are copied onto the report model, and not one field the conformance analyses read is touched.

test.name: recovery_results_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Teardown tolerates a NULL and a zeroed record, so one unconditional release covers every path through the run.

test.name: a_self_call_does_not_block_the_layering
test.purpose: A layered tree holding one self-recursive function still recovers its layering: a self-call orders nothing, and reporting it in place of a layering would repeat what the recursion section already says while costing the analysis this section exists for.

test.name: an_empty_origin_map_knows_and_places_nothing
test.purpose: The two questions the origin map answers are separate calls, and the second is meaningful only where the first is true — a single call returning false would conflate "not in that file" with "no debug information", and a caller making the distinction by accident would exclude every function of an image built without it. NULL is the empty map, and the release is safe twice.

test.name: a_file_the_mapping_describes_is_covered
test.purpose: A file the coverage set names is covered and one it does not name is not — the test that governs every other query in the module.

test.name: an_empty_set_covers_nothing
test.purpose: An image carrying no debug information at all covers no file, so nothing is pruned and the run reports what it reported before this mechanism existed. Null arguments answer the same way rather than faulting.

test.name: a_line_the_mapping_names_was_compiled
test.purpose: Membership at the first line, the last, and one in the middle; a gap between named lines, a line before the first and one past the last all answer not compiled. The binary search is what a heavily repeated line programme is collapsed to, so its boundaries are worth pinning.

test.name: an_uncovered_file_answers_not_compiled_for_every_line
test.purpose: **The failure the two-part contract exists to prevent.** A caller asking only this question would find every line of an uncovered file uncompiled and delete the file. The answer is deliberately the unsafe one; the coverage call is what makes asking it safe, and it has to be asked first.

test.name: several_files_are_each_looked_up_on_their_own_lines
test.purpose: One file's lines are not another's, over a set sorted by path — which is what the binary search over the file table requires.

test.name: a_covered_file_with_no_lines_compiled_nothing
test.purpose: Covered and empty is a different claim from uncovered, and both are representable: the mapping described this file and recorded no instruction for any line of it.

test.name: free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Releasing a null set does not fault and releasing one twice does not double-free, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: reading_a_null_image_yields_an_empty_set
test.purpose: Not a failure. An image with no debug information is ordinary and HLR-141 forbids requiring it, so the set comes back empty and the run proceeds at function granularity alone.

test.name: an_unencoded_name_is_returned_unchanged
test.purpose: The C case and the `extern "C"` case alike: a linkage name nothing encoded is its source name, and returning it unchanged is the whole of the rule.

test.name: the_scheme_is_detected_from_the_name
test.purpose: Nothing in the input says which language produced the symbol. An image does not record that, and a mixed-language image is ordinary, so the scheme is read from the name itself.

test.name: a_decoded_name_is_reduced_to_its_identifier
test.purpose: A qualification, a signature, a cv qualifier, a constructor, a destructor's tilde, and a template's leading return type — the report presents the identifier alone, so both sides of the comparison are reduced to it.

test.name: a_rust_legacy_hash_suffix_is_not_the_name
test.purpose: Rust's legacy scheme ends in a disambiguating hash, which is no path component a reader would recognise. A hash-shaped component of the wrong length is an ordinary name, so the rule cannot be "drop the last component".

test.name: an_undecodable_scheme_resolves_to_nothing
test.purpose: Rust's v0 mangling, which the Itanium demangler rejects, resolves to nothing and is counted rather than matched against a guess.

test.name: an_operator_keeps_its_name
test.purpose: An operator's punctuation is part of its name. The reduction steps over the token whole, or the angle brackets of `operator>>` unbalance the scan and the qualification is never stripped.

test.name: the_source_name_is_reduced_before_it_is_compared
test.purpose: Both sides of the comparison are reduced, so `Widget::size` in the source meets `_ZNK6Widget4sizeEv` in the image. Reducing only the image's side would make every qualified source name a mismatch.

test.name: every_member_of_the_set_is_found
test.purpose: Membership is a binary search over the sorted set, so every member is found wherever it sits in it and a name that is not a member is not.

test.name: an_empty_set_answers_without_searching
test.purpose: An empty set answers no rather than searching a null array, which is undefined however empty it is. The sanitized gate is what makes that a test rather than a comment.

test.name: an_absent_image_fails_and_owns_nothing
test.purpose: An image that is not there is a diagnosed failure that leaves nothing behind to release, so a fatal path exits as leak-clean as a successful one.

test.name: a_file_that_is_not_an_object_file_fails
test.purpose: A source file named where an image was meant fails the same way, rather than being read as an image and yielding an empty set that would filter everything away.

test.name: wrap_passes_through_when_not_armed
test.purpose: An unarmed link-time wrapper delegates to the real implementation, so wrapping does not perturb tests that do not use it.

test.name: wrap_intercepts_when_armed
test.purpose: An armed wrapper intercepts the call, proving the mechanism by which later phases provoke allocation failure.

test.name: help_short_option_reports_help
test.purpose: `-h` is reported as a help request rather than parsed as an ordinary option.

test.name: help_long_option_reports_help
test.purpose: `--help` is reported as a help request.

test.name: unrecognised_option_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: An unrecognised option is rejected as a usage error.

test.name: missing_target_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: An invocation with no target is rejected as a usage error.

test.name: single_target_is_collected
test.purpose: A single target argument is collected into the options structure.

test.name: several_targets_are_collected_in_order
test.purpose: Several targets are collected in argument order, files and directories intermixed.

test.name: help_takes_precedence_over_a_target
test.purpose: A help request is reported without validating the remaining arguments.

test.name: mode_defaults_to_analyse
test.purpose: The run mode defaults to analysis when no mode-selecting option is given.

test.name: the_output_destination_defaults_to_standard_output
test.purpose: A null output path records standard output as the destination when none was supplied.

test.name: an_output_path_is_collected
test.purpose: An output file path is collected into the options, and its argument is not mistaken for a target.

test.name: the_short_output_option_behaves_as_the_long_one
test.purpose: The short form of the redirection option is parsed as the long form is.

test.name: an_output_option_without_its_argument_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: An option requiring an argument and given none is a usage error.

test.name: the_complexity_threshold_defaults_to_fifteen
test.purpose: The threshold defaults to the documented value when none is supplied.

test.name: a_complexity_threshold_is_collected
test.purpose: A threshold given as a long option is collected, and its argument is not mistaken for a target.

test.name: the_short_threshold_option_behaves_as_the_long_one
test.purpose: The short form is parsed as the long form is.

test.name: a_threshold_of_zero_is_accepted
test.purpose: Zero lists every function, which is a legitimate request and must not be read as absent.

test.name: a_malformed_threshold_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: A sign, a trailing tail, leading whitespace, an empty string, and a hexadecimal literal are each rejected — every one of which a permissive conversion would accept, silently yielding a threshold the user did not write.

test.name: options_free_is_safe_on_null
test.purpose: Releasing a null options structure does not fault, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: a_scope_declaration_is_parsed_into_a_name_and_patterns
test.purpose: A name:glob[,glob…] declaration yields the scope name and each component pattern separately.

test.name: scope_declarations_accumulate
test.purpose: The option is repeatable and each declaration adds a scope rather than replacing the last.

test.name: a_malformed_scope_declaration_is_rejected
test.purpose: A scope with no name, a name with no components, and an empty pattern between separators are each a usage error rather than a scope matching nothing — which would report nothing and read as a clean result.

test.name: the_scope_option_reaches_the_options_structure
test.purpose: --scope is parsed by cli_parse into the options structure the analyses read.

test.name: a_malformed_scope_option_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: A malformed --scope argument fails the parse rather than being ignored.

test.name: no_scope_declared_leaves_the_list_empty
test.purpose: An empty scope list means the analysis is omitted with a stated reason, not that every file belongs to one scope.

test.name: a_stratum_declaration_is_parsed_into_a_name_and_patterns
test.purpose: A name:glob[,glob…] declaration yields the layer name and each component pattern separately.

test.name: the_declared_order_fixes_the_ordinals
test.purpose: Declaration order is the permitted dependency direction until an explicit order says otherwise: the first layer named is the top.

test.name: repeating_a_stratum_name_adds_patterns_to_that_layer
test.purpose: One layer of two patterns, not two layers — a second layer of the same name would shift every ordinal below it and change what the layering is measured against.

test.name: a_malformed_stratum_declaration_is_rejected
test.purpose: A layer with no name, a name with no components, and an empty pattern between separators are each a usage error rather than a layer matching nothing.

test.name: stratum_order_reassigns_the_ordinals
test.purpose: An explicit order overrides declaration order, and is applied to the layers already parsed.

test.name: stratum_order_may_precede_the_layers_it_orders
test.purpose: The order is resolved once after every option has been read, so the two options may be given in either sequence.

test.name: stratum_order_naming_an_undeclared_layer_is_an_error
test.purpose: A typo whose silent acceptance would leave the layering validated against something other than what was written.

test.name: a_partial_stratum_order_is_an_error
test.purpose: A partial order determines no direction, and completing it silently would invent one.

test.name: stratum_order_without_any_stratum_is_an_error
test.purpose: An order over no layers orders nothing, and is a usage error rather than a no-op.

test.name: the_bottleneck_threshold_defaults_to_five
test.purpose: The bottleneck threshold defaults to 5 when none is supplied.

test.name: the_bottleneck_threshold_is_configurable
test.purpose: The threshold is user-configurable, as the requirement asks.

test.name: a_malformed_bottleneck_threshold_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: A sign, a trailing tail, leading whitespace and a hexadecimal prefix are each rejected, as they are for the complexity threshold.

test.name: a_rule_argument_is_recorded_unsplit
test.purpose: The `lang:path` argument reaches the options as given. The parser does not split it, and deliberately: whether the named language exists is the registry's question, and answering it here would put a second copy of that knowledge in the option parser.

test.name: rule_arguments_accumulate
test.purpose: The option is repeatable and a second use does not replace the first.

test.name: no_rule_is_supplied_by_default
test.purpose: elc ships no rule of its own beyond the catalogued metrics and thresholds, so an invocation naming none has none.

test.name: a_definition_is_recorded_as_given
test.purpose: A definition reaches the options as given, `NAME` and `NAME=VALUE` alike. What one *means* belongs to the evaluation, which alone knows what a language's conditions can test.

test.name: definitions_are_empty_by_default
test.purpose: With no definitions nothing prunes, which is how adding the option changes no existing result.

test.name: an_empty_definition_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: `-D` with an empty argument names no symbol and is rejected rather than recorded as one.

test.name: a_definition_with_regeneration_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: Pruning happens when a file is measured, so a saved record already describes one configuration and cannot be re-cut into another.

test.name: regeneration_without_a_definition_is_accepted
test.purpose: The boundary of the rule above: regeneration alone is ordinary, and only an explicit definition conflicts with it.

test.name: an_image_path_is_recorded_unvalidated
test.purpose: The path reaches the options as given and nothing is opened. Whether the file is an image elc can read belongs to the module that owns the failure; answering it in the parser would put a second copy of that knowledge there.

test.name: no_image_is_the_default
test.purpose: With no `--elf` the image path is null, which is how adding the option changes no existing result.

test.name: an_empty_image_path_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: An empty argument names no file, so there is nothing for the reader of the image to diagnose and the parser rejects it itself.

test.name: an_image_with_regeneration_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: The filter is applied when a file is measured, so a saved record already describes one filtered run and cannot be re-cut against another image. Rejected rather than silently ignored.

test.name: the_usage_summary_documents_the_image_option
test.purpose: The summary names the option and states that no image means no filtering. The documentation test checks the manual and man page against this text, so this is where the claim itself is made.

test.name: an_output_extension_selects_the_format
test.purpose: Each recognised extension resolves to its own format with no format option given, driven as a table so a format added to the mapping without a case here is visible.

test.name: an_unrecognised_output_extension_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: `-o report.json` is rejected rather than defaulted to the table, which would write a file whose name promises JSON and whose contents are not.

test.name: an_output_path_with_no_extension_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: The four spellings of "no extension": a bare name, a dotfile, a trailing dot, and a name whose only dot is in a directory component. Each names no format and is rejected.

test.name: a_format_option_contradicting_the_filename_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: Driven in both argument orders, because the comparison happens after the option loop rather than as the options arrive; an implementation comparing them in place would pass one order and fail the other.

test.name: a_format_option_agreeing_with_the_filename_is_accepted
test.purpose: Nothing is ambiguous about saying a thing twice, so the agreeing pair parses and yields the format both named.

test.name: the_format_defaults_to_the_table
test.purpose: The default has to survive a resolution step that now runs whether or not anything selected a format, so it is asserted directly rather than left implied by the tests that do select one.

test.name: standard_output_takes_its_format_from_the_option_alone
test.purpose: With no output path there is no extension to resolve, so the option decides and the destination stays standard output.

test.name: regenerating_into_a_filename_naming_a_table_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: An output extension is an explicit format selection, so regeneration rejects one naming anything but Markdown exactly as it rejects `-f table`.

test.name: regenerating_into_a_filename_naming_markdown_is_accepted
test.purpose: The complement, and what stops the rule above from rejecting every `--output` in regeneration mode.

test.name: the_summary_is_the_default_verbosity
test.purpose: A parsed command line with no verbosity option leaves the flag clear, so a zeroed options structure means the composition a run presents when nothing was asked for.

test.name: verbose_is_recorded_in_either_spelling
test.purpose: Both the short and the long spelling reach the options structure.

test.name: verbose_with_a_complete_record_format_is_accepted
test.purpose: The pairing that is not a usage error. Both the request and the format survive the parse for XML and for CSV alike, so the acceptance is a property of the rule rather than of one format.

test.name: the_matrix_companion_is_off_unless_requested
test.purpose: A zeroed configuration means no companion, as it does for the GraphML export.

test.name: the_matrix_companion_is_requested_without_an_output_path
test.purpose: Recorded, not validated against `--output`. Asking for the matrix with the report on standard output writes no file and is not a usage error; rejecting it would make the invocation fail where the requirement says it should quietly produce no companion.

test.name: the_matrix_companion_is_accepted_with_regeneration
test.purpose: Where `--graphml` is rejected with `--from-xml`, this one is accepted: a saved record carries the matrix where it carries no graph, so there is something to write from.

test.name: the_usage_summary_documents_verbosity_and_the_extension_rule
test.purpose: The summary names the verbosity option and states that an output filename's extension selects the format. The documentation test checks both delivered documents against this text, so this is where the claim itself is made. Reading the text back out of a caller-supplied stream is also what establishes that the summary is written to the stream it was handed rather than to a fixed one.

test.name: the_purification_thresholds_default_to_elcs_own
test.purpose: With none supplied the five purification thresholds take the defaults that make purification mean anything at all — a zeroed set would classify every function as everything.

test.name: every_purification_threshold_is_configurable
test.purpose: Each of the five is settable, because a heuristic that cannot be adjusted is one whose disagreements have nowhere to go.

test.name: a_rank_threshold_above_one_hundred_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: A rank is a percentage of the other functions, so a figure above 100 names a position no function can occupy and is rejected rather than silently classifying nothing.

test.name: a_rank_threshold_of_one_hundred_is_accepted
test.purpose: The boundary itself is legitimate: a function outranking every other is what a strict reading of "high authority" asks for.

test.name: a_malformed_purification_threshold_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: A core depth that is not a plain decimal number consumed in its entirety is a usage error, exactly as every other numeric option argument is.

test.name: no_manifest_is_read_without_the_option
test.purpose: A zeroed run names no manifest and requests neither companion: the option is the only way a manifest is reached, which is where the zero-configuration guarantee lives in this structure.

test.name: the_manifest_path_is_taken_from_the_command_line
test.purpose: The path is recorded as given and borrowed from argv rather than copied or opened — the parser reads argv and not files.

test.name: the_manifest_and_drawing_companions_are_requests
test.purpose: Both companion switches are recorded without being validated against --output, by the rule the GraphML export already follows.

test.name: the_recovery_companions_are_refused_in_regeneration_mode
test.purpose: A manifest read, a manifest write, and a request for the drawings are each a usage error combined with --from-xml, so a user who asked for a file and would receive none is told why.

test.name: entry_points_accumulate_across_occurrences
test.purpose: A second --entry adds a root rather than replacing the first, and the symbols are borrowed from argv rather than copied — only the array holding them is owned.

test.name: no_entry_point_leaves_the_set_empty
test.purpose: What makes reachability and depth omit themselves with a reason rather than measure from a root elc chose for the user.

test.name: the_graphml_export_is_a_flag_taking_no_path
test.purpose: The argument following --graphml is the target. A flag that took a path would have swallowed it, and the companion's name is derived from the report rather than given (HLR-119).

test.name: the_call_tree_is_on_unless_declined
test.purpose: Default-on is the whole of HLR-103: the option declines the call tree rather than requesting it, and takes no argument.

test.name: the_environment_variable_names_the_runtime_location
test.purpose: The environment variable names the runtime location, and wins over the path adjacent to the executable — which for a unit binary does not exist at all.

test.name: an_absent_runtime_location_is_fatal
test.purpose: A runtime location that does not exist ends the run: no analysis is possible without one.

test.name: a_runtime_location_that_is_a_file_is_fatal
test.purpose: A runtime location that is a regular file is the same unusable state as a missing one, and is treated the same way.

test.name: an_extension_map_naming_no_language_is_fatal
test.purpose: An extension map naming no language leaves nothing that can be routed to a module, which is the state HLR-036 calls fatal.

test.name: the_extension_map_is_runtime_data
test.purpose: Pointing an unrelated extension at a language resolves, and an extension the data does not name does not — so the mapping is read from runtime data rather than compiled in.

test.name: the_extension_map_tolerates_comments_and_bare_extensions
test.purpose: Comments and blank lines are not entries, an extension written without its leading period still matches, and matching ignores case.

test.name: a_module_is_loaded_on_first_use_of_its_extension
test.purpose: A file's language comes from its extension alone, and first use loads the grammar and compiles all six queries.

test.name: a_language_is_loaded_at_most_once
test.purpose: A second lookup returns the cached module, so a language is loaded at most once per run and a mixed-language target needs one pass.

test.name: an_unmapped_extension_yields_no_module
test.purpose: An extension the map does not name, and a file name with no extension at all, both yield no module — so the caller skips rather than fails.

test.name: an_absent_grammar_makes_the_language_unusable
test.purpose: A module whose grammar is missing is excluded rather than fatal, and opening the registry does not load any grammar up front.

test.name: a_missing_query_file_makes_the_language_unusable
test.purpose: A module omitting one of the six required query files is handled as unusable, not as undefined behaviour.

test.name: an_invalid_query_makes_the_language_unusable
test.purpose: A query file that will not compile makes its language unusable rather than crashing the run or being silently ignored.

test.name: an_unusable_language_is_not_retried
test.purpose: A language that failed to load is recorded once, so the diagnostic is emitted once rather than once per file that would have used it.

test.name: no_particular_language_is_required
test.purpose: The registry opens over whatever the runtime location holds and verifies no particular language up front.

test.name: close_is_safe_on_null_and_on_a_zeroed_registry
test.purpose: Teardown is safe on a null and on a never-opened registry, so every error path can release unconditionally.

test.name: a_located_rule_is_bound_by_its_directory
test.purpose: A rule under queries/<lang>/rules/ is bound to that language with nothing naming it, and its identity's first half is the basename with the extension removed.

test.name: a_broken_located_rule_is_excluded_and_the_run_continues
test.purpose: A rule in the runtime location that will not compile is a malformed component: diagnosed, excluded, and survived rather than kept or fatal.

test.name: a_broken_located_rule_does_not_exclude_its_neighbours
test.purpose: One broken rule does not take a good one with it, which a loader abandoning the directory on first failure would do.

test.name: a_broken_named_rule_fails_the_run
test.purpose: The same failure from the command line is a user error and stops the run. Paired with the located case above, this is the provenance rule itself rather than either half of it.

test.name: an_absent_named_rule_fails_the_run
test.purpose: An unreadable named rule fails exactly as an uncompilable one does: the provenance decides, not the kind of failure.

test.name: a_rule_for_an_unavailable_language_is_skipped_not_fatal
test.purpose: A rule naming a language with no module is reported and skipped rather than compiled, and is not fatal even from the command line — what is missing is the module, not the rule.

test.name: a_rule_argument_without_a_language_fails
test.purpose: An argument with no language is a usage error rather than a path silently taken for a language name.

test.name: no_rule_is_discovered_from_the_working_directory
test.purpose: A rule sitting in the working directory is not a rule. Two users running the same command on the same tree must obtain the same result.

test.name: physical_lines_are_counted
test.purpose: The physical line count comes from the mapped contents.

test.name: an_unterminated_final_line_counts
test.purpose: A trailing fragment with no terminating newline is a line the reader sees, and is counted as one.

test.name: a_zero_length_file_reports_zero_without_error
test.purpose: A file of zero length reports zero metrics without error, rather than being mapped — mmap of an empty file fails with EINVAL.

test.name: an_unreadable_file_is_a_failure_without_metrics
test.purpose: A file that cannot be read yields a failure and no metrics for the caller to release, so the run continues leak-free.

test.name: the_metrics_carry_the_path_and_language
test.purpose: The returned metrics carry the path measured and the language resolved for it.

test.name: a_function_is_reported_with_its_name_and_line_range
test.purpose: A function is reported with its name and its line range, the span beginning at the signature rather than at the body's opening brace.

test.name: a_nested_function_is_reported_in_its_own_right
test.purpose: A named function declared inside another is reported as a function of its own, with its own name and line range, rather than folded into its enclosing function.

test.name: a_prototype_is_not_a_function
test.purpose: A declaration without a body contributes no function: what counts as one is the query file's decision, and it supplies no body capture for a prototype.

test.name: a_function_name_outlives_the_mapping
test.purpose: A name is still readable after analyze_file returns, so it was copied out of the mapping rather than pointed into it.

test.name: an_unmapped_extension_is_a_skip_not_a_failure
test.purpose: A file whose extension maps to no language is a skip, a distinct outcome from a failure, so the exit status stays 0.

test.name: spans_are_sorted_before_merging
test.purpose: Spans arriving out of order are sorted before anything is merged, and disjoint spans stay separate.

test.name: overlapping_spans_coalesce
test.purpose: Two spans that overlap become one covering both, so their shared lines are counted once.

test.name: a_nested_span_is_absorbed_not_counted_twice
test.purpose: A span wholly inside another is absorbed and contributes nothing of its own — the canonical case of a block comment carrying inline comment syntax, where subtracting per capture counts its lines twice.

test.name: a_shared_line_is_counted_once
test.purpose: A line shared by three comments is one line, however many spans touch it. Counting per span is what drives ELOC below zero.

test.name: coalescing_a_trailing_run_stays_in_bounds
test.purpose: Coalescing a run of spans that reaches the last element stops there. The bound is the whole of the requirement: without it the loop reads one past the final span whenever the trailing run is longer than one.

test.name: merging_an_empty_span_list_is_zero
test.purpose: A file with no comments merges to nothing without touching an empty array.

test.name: the_narrowest_enclosing_function_wins
test.purpose: A statement inside a nested function is attributed to that function rather than to the one enclosing it.

test.name: the_narrowest_wins_whatever_order_the_ranges_are_in
test.purpose: The answer does not depend on the order the ranges were discovered in — an implementation returning the first containing range would also break determinism.

test.name: an_offset_outside_every_function_has_no_owner
test.purpose: An offset outside every function belongs to none, so file-scope code contributes to the file alone; the start offset is inclusive and the end offset exclusive.

test.name: an_empty_range_index_owns_nothing
test.purpose: A file defining no function attributes nothing, rather than indexing an empty array.

test.name: a_multi_line_statement_counts_once
test.purpose: The same expression written across three lines and on one line yields the same ELOC, so layout cannot move the number.

test.name: only_statements_count_toward_eloc
test.purpose: A directive, a lone brace, a bare declaration, and a blank line contribute nothing, while an initialising declaration and a return each contribute one.

test.name: two_statements_on_one_line_count_once
test.purpose: Two statements sharing a line are one line of code. Counting captures instead would make the same two statements worth twice as much on one line as on two.

test.name: a_nested_functions_statements_are_not_counted_twice
test.purpose: A nested function's statements contribute to it alone, the enclosing function keeps only its own, and the file counts each line once.

test.name: file_scope_code_counts_for_the_file_only
test.purpose: An initialised global contributes to the file's ELOC and to no function's.

test.name: a_file_with_nothing_executable_reports_zero_eloc
test.purpose: A file of comments, directives, and bare declarations reports zero ELOC without error.

test.name: a_trailing_comment_does_not_remove_its_line
test.purpose: A line of code carrying a trailing comment is still a line of code. The exclusion is byte-granular for this reason; a line-granular one deletes the statement.

test.name: a_function_that_never_branches_is_one
test.purpose: A function with no decision point reports 1. A query capturing the function itself would report 2, which is the failure this asserts against.

test.name: each_decision_point_adds_one
test.purpose: Two decision points make three, so the base and the increment are both applied exactly once.

test.name: a_nested_functions_decisions_are_not_counted_twice
test.purpose: A nested named function owns its decision points and the function enclosing it gains none of them; running the query against the enclosing body without attribution would report one more.

test.name: an_unreported_scope_attributes_to_the_named_function_around_it
test.purpose: An offset inside a scope that is not a reported function resolves to the nearest named function containing it. This is the anonymous-callable rule, whose language-level observable waits for a language with lambdas; the mechanism it constrains is verified here.

test.name: a_file_scope_decision_belongs_to_no_function
test.purpose: A conditional in a file-scope initialiser is charged to no function rather than to an arbitrary one.

test.name: filemetrics_free_is_safe_on_null
test.purpose: Releasing a null metrics structure does not fault, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: statements_after_a_terminator_are_recorded
test.purpose: The named siblings following a captured terminator are recorded as unreachable, with the after-terminator cause.

test.name: a_label_after_a_terminator_is_not_recorded
test.purpose: A goto label following a return is a sibling of it and is reachable. Recording it would be a false claim inviting the deletion of a live branch target — the single case that decides whether this analysis can be trusted.

test.name: a_branch_guarded_by_a_variable_is_never_recorded
test.purpose: A condition holding a variable is not claimed dead however evidently its value could be inferred: deciding it needs data flow, and elc performs none.

test.name: a_literal_branch_is_recorded_with_its_whole_span
test.purpose: The branch a literal condition excludes is recorded as its full line range, because the span is what the reader deletes.

test.name: a_predicate_that_does_not_hold_rejects_the_match
test.purpose: A query predicate is evaluated rather than ignored. The parser library returns predicates as data, so without evaluation every conditional would match the literal-condition pattern.

test.name: a_dead_span_is_attributed_to_the_innermost_function
test.purpose: Each recorded span belongs to the reported function containing it, by the rule ELOC and complexity already use.

test.name: a_language_with_no_dead_code_query_is_unanalysed_not_clean
test.purpose: A language module supplying no dead-code query records that the analysis was not performed, rather than recording that no dead code was found.

test.name: a_partly_unparsable_file_is_measured_around_the_damage
test.purpose: A file with a recoverable error yields the metrics of its sound parts, including the function *after* the damaged region — recovering only what precedes it would leave the back of every damaged file unmeasured.

test.name: damage_that_swallows_the_rest_of_a_file_is_counted_as_such
test.purpose: An unbalanced delimiter leaves the parser nothing to resynchronise on, so what follows is genuinely lost. The property under test is that the reported line count covers what was destroyed, so the reader is not misled about the function count.

test.name: a_damaged_file_is_a_degraded_outcome_not_a_clean_one
test.purpose: A partly unparsed file is an outcome distinct from a clean analysis, so its metrics are used and the run is still counted against the exit status.

test.name: a_sound_file_reports_no_damage
test.purpose: Paired with the tests above so that an implementation reporting damage everywhere cannot pass them.

test.name: damage_is_counted_in_distinct_lines
test.purpose: Two unparsable constructs on one line are one line, by the rule the comment exclusion already counts by.

test.name: the_macro_concatenation_the_c_grammar_cannot_follow_is_survivable
test.purpose: The exact idiom that prompted the change: tree-sitter-c accepts one identifier before the first string literal of a concatenation and not two, so the ANSI-colour macro convention common in embedded C does not parse. One line of damage, and the functions around it measured.

test.name: a_dead_span_outside_every_function_is_not_recorded
test.purpose: HLR-137 asks about statements within a function, and a span outside every one of them has no enclosing function to be reported against — so it would reach the report with a blank where the attribution goes.

test.name: fan_out_counts_distinct_callees
test.purpose: Four call sites to two functions give a fan-out of two, so the measure is of subroutines invoked and not of invocations.

test.name: fan_out_ignores_global_edges
test.purpose: A function that writes a global another reads has a fan-out of zero: coupling through shared state is not invocation.

test.name: fan_in_counts_distinct_callers
test.purpose: Three call sites from two functions give a fan-in of two, so the measure is of callers and not of invocations; a function nothing calls reports zero.

test.name: fan_in_ignores_global_edges
test.purpose: A function that reads a global another writes has a fan-in of zero. The converse of the fan-out case: the global edge runs towards the reader, so an in-degree over the whole SDG would count a writer as a caller and inflate a figure that is banded.

test.name: the_degrees_are_counted_over_a_wide_hub
test.purpose: Both degrees are counted correctly at a size no fixture tree reaches, and at a size the bands care about: 300 callers is twelve times the fan-in warning bound and 300 callees twenty times the fan-out critical one, so a counting error here moves a finding rather than merely a figure.

test.name: the_maintainability_index_matches_the_formula
test.purpose: A function of twenty effective lines, complexity five, one caller and two callees scores 66 — the formula worked through by hand from its definition, so an arithmetic change in any of the three terms is caught against the arithmetic rather than against elc's own output.

test.name: the_maintainability_index_handles_its_edges
test.purpose: The three edges the formula reaches: a function with no effective lines takes its length as one rather than putting ln(0) in the third term; either degree being zero makes the flow term vanish, so a wide fan-out costs nothing with no callers; and a function of some millions of lines is clamped at zero rather than reporting a negative score.

test.name: the_maintainability_index_falls_as_a_function_worsens
test.purpose: The index falls when a function is made longer, branchier or more entangled, and never rises. The direction is the whole of what the metric asserts, and a sign error in any term would leave the arithmetic plausible and the meaning inverted.

test.name: direct_recursion_is_detected
test.purpose: A function calling itself is reported as a one-member cycle.

test.name: mutual_recursion_is_detected
test.purpose: A mutually recursive pair is one cycle of two members rather than two cycles of one.

test.name: a_straight_line_program_has_no_cycles
test.purpose: An acyclic call graph reports no recursion, so the trivial single-node components every decomposition produces are not mistaken for self-calls.

test.name: a_global_cycle_is_not_recursion
test.purpose: Two functions each writing a global the other reads form a cycle in the SDG and no recursion at all, which is the case that would otherwise produce a false critical MISRA C Rule 17.2 finding on ordinary code.

test.name: depth_is_the_length_of_the_deepest_chain
test.purpose: A three-function chain from a declared entry point measures three, the entry point counting as the first layer.

test.name: the_deepest_chain_is_an_ordered_sequence
test.purpose: With a shallow branch listed first and a deep one second, the reported chain is the deep one in order — a search taking the first edge would give the wrong path and the wrong length.

test.name: depth_measures_from_the_deepest_entry_point
test.purpose: Given two entry points of different depths, the reported figure and chain are the worst case across them.

test.name: recursion_yields_no_depth_and_terminates
test.purpose: A recursive call graph reports its cycle, no depth figure, and no chain — and the run terminates, which a longest-path search over a cyclic graph would not.

test.name: no_entry_points_omits_depth_with_a_reason
test.purpose: With no declaration the depth analysis is omitted rather than failed, `main` is not inferred despite being present, and the measurements needing no declaration are still produced.

test.name: an_entry_point_matching_nothing_is_a_distinct_omission
test.purpose: A declared entry point naming no analysed function yields a different omission from declaring none, because the two call for different actions.

test.name: depth_carries_the_unresolved_count
test.purpose: The unresolved-call count travels with the depth, since a chain through an unresolved call is not followed and the figure is a lower bound.

test.name: a_chain_does_not_travel_along_a_global_edge
test.purpose: A chain stops at the last function actually called, rather than continuing to one that merely reads a global the callee wrote.

test.name: an_empty_project_measures_nothing_without_failing
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing produces an empty but valid set of measurements.

test.name: tree_results_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Releasing a null or already-released result set does not fault, so teardown is unconditional on every path.

test.name: excluded_extension_matches_the_runtime_list
test.purpose: An extension present in the runtime list is excluded and one absent from it is not, the list having been read from the runtime location rather than from any table in the binary.

test.name: excluded_extension_ignores_case
test.purpose: One entry covers every spelling of an extension, so a list maintained in lower case still excludes an upper-case file name.

test.name: a_name_without_an_extension_is_not_excluded
test.purpose: A dot occurring in a directory component, and a name that is nothing but a suffix, are both correctly read as having no extension to test.

test.name: an_empty_exclusion_list_excludes_nothing
test.purpose: An empty list excludes nothing, which is the state discovery runs in when the runtime file is absent.

test.name: extension_list_skips_comments_and_blank_lines
test.purpose: Comment and blank lines are not entries, and an entry written without its leading period still matches, so the data file can be maintained in either style.

test.name: a_missing_extension_list_is_not_fatal
test.purpose: An absent binary-extension file yields an empty list rather than aborting the run, so discovery still completes.

test.name: a_regular_file_target_is_appended_directly
test.purpose: A target that is a regular file is appended to the file list with no directory traversal performed for it.

test.name: a_missing_target_is_rejected_with_an_empty_list
test.purpose: A target that does not exist is rejected, and no partial file list survives the rejection.

test.name: a_target_that_is_neither_file_nor_directory_is_rejected
test.purpose: A FIFO named as a target is rejected, covering the class of targets that exist but are neither regular file nor directory.

test.name: every_target_is_validated_before_any_is_walked
test.purpose: A valid target given alongside an invalid one is not walked, so a report can never cover fewer targets than the user named.

test.name: a_file_reached_through_two_targets_appears_once
test.purpose: A file named explicitly and also contained in a named directory is retained once, canonicalisation having preceded de-duplication.

test.name: the_file_list_is_sorted_into_byte_order
test.purpose: The completed list is in ascending byte order whatever order the filesystem enumerated it in.

test.name: hidden_entries_and_binary_extensions_are_excluded
test.purpose: A hidden file, a hidden directory's contents, and a file carrying an excluded extension are all absent from the walk's result.

test.name: the_walk_descends_into_subdirectories
test.purpose: The traversal is recursive: a file several directories below the target is found.

test.name: a_hidden_directory_named_as_the_target_is_traversed
test.purpose: The hidden-entry exclusion applies below the target and not to the target itself, so a hidden directory named on the command line is walked.

test.name: files_and_directories_are_classified_independently
test.purpose: Each target is routed on its own type, so a file and a directory given together are both handled correctly.

test.name: a_cyclic_directory_symlink_terminates
test.purpose: A self-referential directory link does not produce an unbounded traversal, and the linked directory is not descended into. Reaching the assertion is itself the result.

test.name: a_symbolic_link_named_as_a_target_is_resolved
test.purpose: A link named directly as a target is resolved to its referent, the other half of the symbolic-link policy from the one the walk applies.

test.name: a_path_that_cannot_be_canonicalised_is_a_per_file_failure
test.purpose: A canonicalisation failure, provoked through a link-time wrapper, drops that path and records a per-file failure rather than ending the run.

test.name: git_walk_yields_the_tracked_files
test.purpose: The walk enumerates the files committed at `HEAD` and not a file that exists in the working tree but was never added, which is the exclusion the route exists to perform.

test.name: git_walk_is_scoped_to_the_target
test.purpose: Naming a subdirectory enumerates that subdirectory alone, though the tree at `HEAD` is the whole repository.

test.name: git_walk_declines_a_directory_in_no_repository
test.purpose: A directory outside any repository is declined rather than failed: nothing is appended, no failure is recorded, and the negative return is what sends the caller to the filesystem walk.

test.name: git_walk_declines_a_target_the_repository_does_not_track
test.purpose: A directory inside a work tree that `HEAD` knows nothing about — a build directory, or a home directory under version control — is declined, so the target is analysed by traversal instead of reported as empty.

test.name: a_tracked_directory_of_excluded_files_stays_on_the_git_route
test.purpose: A tracked directory whose every tracked file is excluded yields nothing and is still judged applicable, so the run does not fall back and analyse the untracked files beside them. Distinguishes "the repository tracks this directory" from "the repository yielded a file".

test.name: a_route_is_recorded_for_each_target
test.purpose: Each target's route is recorded in the order given, naming the same target twice records it once, and releasing the list leaves it usable rather than stale.

test.name: the_route_list_owns_the_target_it_records
test.purpose: Mutating the caller's buffer after recording does not change the record, so the report can outlive the strings discovery was given.

test.name: filelist_free_is_safe_on_null
test.purpose: Releasing a null file list or extension list does not fault, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: roots_are_entry_points_and_address_taken_functions
test.purpose: The root set is the union of the two and nothing else: a function neither declared nor address-taken is not a root.

test.name: a_declared_symbol_naming_nothing_is_skipped_not_fatal
test.purpose: A declared entry point matching no analysed function is skipped rather than failing the run, since analysing one directory of a project whose entry point lives in another is ordinary.

test.name: a_root_declared_twice_is_one_root
test.purpose: The root set is de-duplicated, so a symbol declared twice and also address-taken contributes one root.

test.name: a_clique_of_unused_functions_is_unreachable
test.purpose: Two unused functions calling one another are both reported: each has a caller, so a textual rule finds neither, and no path reaches the pair from any root.

test.name: an_address_taken_function_and_its_callees_are_reachable
test.purpose: An address-taken function is a root rather than an exemption: what it calls is reached through it. An implementation that merely excluded it from the report would report its callee dead.

test.name: reachability_does_not_travel_along_a_global_edge
test.purpose: A function reachable only by reading an object another function wrote is still unreachable: control never travels along a state edge, and following one would rescue genuinely dead code from the report.

test.name: with_no_entry_points_nothing_is_unreachable
test.purpose: With no declaration the analysis is omitted with its reason, and no function is reported unreachable.

test.name: a_declaration_matching_nothing_is_its_own_omission
test.purpose: Declaring an entry point that matches nothing is a different omission from declaring none, because the two call for different actions from the reader.

test.name: a_global_touched_by_one_function_is_a_scope_reduction_candidate
test.purpose: An object one function writes and reads is flagged, and the graph carries no edge for it at all — which is why the finding is computed from the access records rather than from the edge table.

test.name: a_global_spanning_disconnected_regions_is_a_hidden_channel
test.purpose: An object written in one region of the call graph and read in another that never calls it is flagged, with the region count establishing the disconnection.

test.name: shared_state_within_one_region_is_ordinary
test.purpose: The same sharing between two functions joined by a call edge carries no finding. Without this distinction the warning would fire on every shared variable.

test.name: an_undeclared_identifier_is_not_global_state
test.purpose: An identifier no file declares at file scope is not global state, however the over-broad read and write patterns captured it.

test.name: a_global_touched_only_by_dead_functions_is_unreachable
test.purpose: An object every one of whose accessors is unreachable is itself reported unreachable.

test.name: a_global_no_function_touches_is_not_claimed_dead
test.purpose: An object no analysed function accesses is not claimed: it may be touched from file scope or from a translation unit outside the target.

test.name: an_edge_crossing_a_declared_boundary_is_reported
test.purpose: A call from a function in one declared scope to a function in another is reported as a crossing.

test.name: a_shared_global_crossing_a_boundary_is_reported
test.purpose: A scope that never calls into another but writes a variable the other reads has not been isolated. An implementation checking call edges alone would report the arrangement clean.

test.name: a_component_matching_no_declaration_is_outside_the_partition
test.purpose: An edge touching a file no declaration names is not a crossing: inventing a boundary would report violations against a division nobody drew.

test.name: with_no_scopes_declared_the_analysis_is_omitted
test.purpose: With no execution scopes declared the analysis is omitted with its reason rather than reporting an empty result.

test.name: an_empty_graph_analyses_without_incident
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing produces empty state results rather than faulting.

test.name: instability_is_ce_over_the_sum
test.purpose: Instability is efferent coupling divided by the sum of both couplings.

test.name: instability_is_zero_when_nothing_is_depended_upon
test.purpose: A component depending on nothing but depended upon widely is maximally stable, and the value is a real 0 rather than undefined — Ca is not zero, so the division is well formed.

test.name: instability_is_one_when_nothing_depends_on_it
test.purpose: The opposite extreme: freely changeable, because nothing rests on it.

test.name: instability_is_undefined_when_both_couplings_are_zero
test.purpose: No division is performed and the value is reported undefined. A component with no relationships at all is ordinary, and 0, 1 and NaN are all wrong answers for it.

test.name: coupling_counts_components_not_calls
test.purpose: Three calls into one component are one dependency. Counting call sites would treat a file calling another in forty places as depending on forty things.

test.name: a_call_within_one_component_is_no_coupling_at_all
test.purpose: A file does not depend on itself — the same rule that keeps intra-file recursion out of the cycle report.

test.name: a_bottleneck_needs_both_couplings_at_the_threshold
test.purpose: A component is flagged only where afferent and efferent coupling each meet the threshold; a widely-used leaf is stable, not a bottleneck.

test.name: a_cycle_between_two_components_is_found_with_a_loop
test.purpose: The group and a concrete loop through it are both produced, since the group is what must be broken up and the loop is which edge to cut.

test.name: mutual_recursion_within_one_component_is_not_a_cycle
test.purpose: The case HLR-083 names. The call view holds a cycle and the component projection does not, so reporting it would tell an architect to split a file over a function-level recursion finding.

test.name: an_acyclic_projection_yields_no_cycles
test.purpose: A one-directional dependency between two components is not a cycle.

test.name: a_three_component_cycle_reports_its_whole_group
test.purpose: A longer cycle reports every member and a loop visiting all three.

test.name: a_call_descending_two_layers_is_skip_level_only
test.purpose: Bypassing an intervening layer in the declared direction is skip-level and inverts nothing.

test.name: a_call_ascending_one_layer_is_inverted_only
test.purpose: Running against the declared direction without bypassing anything is direction-inverted and is not a skip.

test.name: a_call_ascending_two_layers_is_both
test.purpose: Both statements are true of such a call and each has its own remedy, so it is reported twice rather than folded into one finding.

test.name: a_call_descending_one_layer_is_no_violation
test.purpose: The arrangement the user declared produces nothing. Without this an implementation flagging every inter-layer call would pass every test above.

test.name: a_component_in_no_declared_stratum_is_outside_the_partition
test.purpose: A file no declaration names has nothing to be compared against; placing it would report violations against a design nobody drew.

test.name: with_no_strata_declared_layering_is_omitted
test.purpose: The layering is omitted with its reason, and the coupling table is produced all the same.

test.name: a_state_edge_is_not_a_layering_violation
test.purpose: A global two layers share is a different fact with its own analyses; the dependency is still counted in the coupling table.

test.name: an_empty_graph_analyses_without_incident
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing produces empty architectural results rather than faulting.

test.name: the_indices_count_the_reported_findings_rather_than_the_graph
test.purpose: The indices are formed from a hand-made violation list with no graph anywhere near them. That absence is the test: a function able to produce them from nothing but the recorded findings is the shape HLR-164 asks for, and an implementation that re-derived them from the graph could not compile against the call.

test.name: a_zero_denominator_is_undefined_rather_than_perfect
test.purpose: With no inter-layer call edge both indices are undefined, not 0 — the error HLR-082 already avoids for Instability, arriving here instead as a claim of perfect conformance for a project that has demonstrated nothing.

test.name: a_call_that_both_skips_and_inverts_counts_once_in_each_index
test.purpose: One call ascending two layers makes each index 100% of the single candidate edge, so the two sum to 200%. The assertion that their sum exceeds the denominator is what pins the rule against combining them into one score.

test.name: an_intra_layer_call_is_not_in_the_denominator
test.purpose: One layer holding every component: the call is real and inside it, an edge within a layer has no direction to invert, and the denominator is therefore zero rather than one.

test.name: an_edge_touching_an_unpartitioned_component_is_not_in_the_denominator
test.purpose: A call from a file no declaration names has nothing to be compared against and nothing to count. Including it would put an edge in the denominator no numerator could reach, so every index would drift downward with each undeclared file.

test.name: rows_are_callers_and_columns_are_callees
test.purpose: The orientation asserted directly rather than inferred from a total. A matrix built the other way round is still a square grid of plausible numbers, and every reading taken from it is exactly backwards.

test.name: back_calls_gather_below_the_diagonal
test.purpose: The sum of the cells below the diagonal is compared against the back-call count the conformance indices report over the same tree, so the grid and the list are pinned as two views of one fact.

test.name: subjects_follow_the_layer_index_not_the_declaration_order
test.purpose: The permutation `--stratum-order` leaves behind moves a subject in the sequence, and the call that ascended two layers moves above the diagonal. Ordering by declaration order instead would put the back-calls above it for every project using the option.

test.name: with_no_strata_the_subjects_are_the_directories
test.purpose: The fallback that makes the matrix useful to the reader who has declared nothing, which is most readers on a first run.

test.name: directories_are_ordered_by_path_not_by_component_order
test.purpose: `/p/a-b/x.c` sorts before `/p/a/y.c` because `-` precedes `/`, yet `/p/a` precedes `/p/a-b`. Reading the directories off in component order would produce a sequence no rule describes — and one two runs over the same tree would agree on, so no determinism test would catch it.

test.name: a_component_outside_every_stratum_reaches_no_cell
test.purpose: With only the middle layer declared every call touches a file it does not name, so the grid is one subject wide and entirely empty.

test.name: a_shared_global_is_not_a_matrix_cell
test.purpose: A global object two subjects share is coupling and not invocation. Counting one would put a number below the diagonal that no call put there.

test.name: repeated_calls_to_one_callee_are_one_edge
test.purpose: A cell counts distinct call edges rather than call sites, which is the figure the conformance denominator is also over. A cell counting sites would disagree with the percentages printed above it.

test.name: every_rendering_states_the_convention
test.purpose: All three decorations carry the same orientation sentence. A matrix whose orientation the reader must infer conveys the opposite of what it is for half the time.

test.name: an_empty_matrix_still_renders
test.purpose: An empty grid renders as its heading, its convention, and its column names rather than as nothing. A section that vanishes when it has no content makes the report's shape vary with its content.

test.name: a_comma_in_a_subject_is_quoted_in_the_csv
test.purpose: A directory carrying a comma is quoted by the same `write_field` the per-function renderer uses; the negative assertion pins that an unquoted one would have split the row.

test.name: a_pipe_in_a_subject_is_escaped_in_the_markdown
test.purpose: GFM ends a cell at an unescaped pipe, so a directory carrying one would shift every cell to its right by a column — a grid that still parses and says something else.

test.name: the_markdown_columns_are_measured_after_escaping
test.purpose: Every row of the grid is the same width with an escaped subject in it. A column measured before escaping comes out a character short for every pipe in it.

test.name: the_companion_is_written_only_when_asked_and_named
test.purpose: Off unless requested, nothing without an output path to derive a name from, and — unlike the two graph companions — still warranted in regeneration mode, a record carrying the matrix where it carries no topology.

test.name: free_is_safe_on_null_and_on_a_zeroed_matrix
test.purpose: Teardown is unconditional on every exit path, so releasing a matrix that was never built must not fault and must not free twice.

test.name: the_fan_out_bands_match_the_published_table
test.purpose: Each of the eight boundary values from PVD Appendix A.2 bands as the table says. The same eight are pinned as measurements by calltree/fanout.c, so a disagreement here is a banding error rather than a counting one.

test.name: the_acceptable_band_produces_no_finding
test.purpose: A fan-out of 9 is acceptable and silent. This band was a gap in an earlier reading of the thresholds, which is why exhaustiveness is stated rather than inferred.

test.name: every_fan_out_value_classifies_exactly_once
test.purpose: Exhaustiveness as a property rather than as cases: every value from 0 to 40 lands in exactly one band, with none skipped and none claimed twice.

test.name: every_measurement_names_a_source
test.purpose: Every measurement kind names a non-empty source. Asserted over the kinds rather than over the catalogue because what must never happen is a kind reaching a reader with a band and no citation for it.

test.name: every_banded_measurement_names_its_source_in_its_row
test.purpose: The citation a banded measurement carries comes from its catalogue row, so the table a reviewer reads is the table elc reports from.

test.name: complexity_is_banded_on_a_published_authority
test.purpose: Complexity warns above 10 and is critical above 15, on McCabe's authority as NIST SP 500-235 records it; 10 is inside the accepted range and 15 the top of the warning band rather than the bottom of the critical one, and the row is not marked as elc's own.

test.name: fan_in_is_banded_on_elcs_own_authority_and_says_so
test.purpose: Fan-in warns above 25, carries the label saying the threshold is elc's own rather than a published standard, and has no critical band however large the value.

test.name: an_occurrence_row_bands_no_counted_value
test.purpose: A row whose finding is its mere occurrence, and a kind the catalogue holds no row for, both answer "no band" to the counted question — so a count is never put through bounds that would report every non-zero value as critical.

test.name: maintainability_is_banded_downwards_on_elcs_own_authority
test.purpose: The one catalogue row that runs the other way: a value strictly below a bound falls in the band, the bounds read as the numbers a reader is looking for rather than as their complements, and the row is marked as elc's own — the SEI's 85 and 65 were calibrated for a formula with a Halstead term this one does not have. Asserts too that inverting one row did not invert the others.

test.name: exactly_three_thresholds_are_elcs_own_and_say_so
test.purpose: Exactly three thresholds are not published standards — the bottleneck heuristic, the fan-in band, and the maintainability bands — and each says so where a reader sees it. Asserting the count means a fourth could only appear by decision rather than by drift.

test.name: the_published_thresholds_are_not_marked_as_elcs_own
test.purpose: The published rows cite MISRA and Martin and carry no elc marker, so the label distinguishes rather than decorating everything.

test.name: a_kind_outside_the_catalogue_yields_no_entry
test.purpose: A measurement kind the catalogue does not hold returns no entry, so the caller reports a bare value rather than discarding it or inventing a band.

test.name: the_severity_set_is_closed_and_ordered
test.purpose: The three names are exactly the closed set, and their ranks order info below warning below critical — the ordering that 'the highest applicable band wins' is defined against.

test.name: an_unrecognised_severity_ranks_lowest_rather_than_faulting
test.purpose: A name outside the set, and a null one, rank lowest instead of faulting the ordering.

test.name: the_highest_applicable_band_is_the_one_reported
test.purpose: A value above both bounds produces one finding at the higher severity, not two findings or the lower one.

test.name: every_finding_carries_exactly_one_severity
test.purpose: No finding is emitted without a severity, and none carries a value outside the closed set.

test.name: call_depth_bands_at_eight_and_twelve
test.purpose: Depth bands against the embedded guidance: 8 is within it, 9 warns, 12 warns, 13 is critical.

test.name: an_omitted_depth_is_not_banded_as_zero
test.purpose: A depth omitted for want of an entry point is not banded at all. Banding it would judge a number that does not exist.

test.name: a_clean_project_yields_no_findings
test.purpose: Finding nothing is an ordinary result. Paired with every band test so that an implementation emitting findings unconditionally cannot pass them.

test.name: findinglist_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Releasing an empty or already-released finding list does not fault.

test.name: every_discovered_function_becomes_a_node
test.purpose: Every function across every analysed file receives a node, so the graph spans the project rather than any one file.

test.name: node_identifiers_follow_sorted_file_order
test.purpose: Files handed over in unsorted order still number their functions by sorted path, so node identifiers are a property of the source tree and not of discovery order.

test.name: a_call_resolves_across_files
test.purpose: A call whose definition lies in another file resolves to an edge, which is the cross-file resolution the graph exists to perform.

test.name: repeated_calls_collapse_to_one_edge_with_a_count
test.purpose: Three call sites between one pair of functions produce one edge carrying a count of three, so out-degree is distinct callees rather than call sites.

test.name: an_unresolvable_call_is_counted_and_does_not_abort
test.purpose: A call into a library is counted, produces no edge, and does not fail the build — no destination is invented for it, which is what keeps a later dead-code proof sound.

test.name: a_call_from_file_scope_has_no_caller_node
test.purpose: A call outside every reported function draws no edge and is counted as unresolved, because the graph does not represent it and the reader is judging completeness.

test.name: a_global_links_its_writer_to_its_reader
test.purpose: A global written in one file and read in another produces an edge between the two functions, and that edge names the object through the graph's own copy of the string.

test.name: an_undeclared_name_is_not_global_state
test.purpose: An identifier written in one function and read in another, declared nowhere at file scope, produces no edge — the over-broad capture is resolved away rather than believed.

test.name: two_objects_between_one_pair_are_two_edges
test.purpose: Global edges are per object and do not collapse the way call edges do, since merging them would lose which shared state couples the two functions.

test.name: an_address_taken_function_is_marked
test.purpose: A function assigned without being called is marked as a reachability root, captured in this phase though Phase 10 is what consumes it.

test.name: an_address_taken_name_that_is_not_a_function_is_discarded
test.purpose: An ordinary variable captured by the deliberately over-broad address-taken patterns resolves to nothing and marks no node, which is what allows the query files not to decide.

test.name: the_component_projection_is_file_level
test.purpose: A call between functions in two files yields one component edge between those files, a component being a source file.

test.name: a_call_within_one_file_is_no_component_dependency
test.purpose: A call inside one file adds no component edge, so a file is not recorded as depending on itself.

test.name: an_empty_project_builds_an_empty_graph
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing builds a valid empty graph, including the library structure, rather than failing or leaving a null handle.

test.name: the_library_returns_errors_instead_of_aborting
test.purpose: Asking a cyclic graph for a topological ordering returns an error rather than aborting the process, so the library's default abort-on-error handler has been replaced. Reaching the assertion is itself the result: without the handler the test dies rather than fails.

test.name: graph_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Releasing a null or an already-released graph does not fault, so teardown is unconditional on every exit path.

test.name: dot_is_written_without_being_asked_for
test.purpose: A zeroed ElcOptions with an output path warrants the companion: generation is enabled by default, which is the one place the `.dot` default runs opposite to GraphML's.

test.name: dot_is_suppressed_by_the_disable_switch
test.purpose: The disable switch turns the default off.

test.name: dot_needs_an_output_path
test.purpose: With the report going to standard output nothing is warranted, there being no path to derive the companion's name from.

test.name: dot_needs_an_output_path_even_when_disabled
test.purpose: "Whether or not generation was disabled" is the requirement's wording: the destination decides it and the switch cannot change the answer, so both paths are asserted rather than one.

test.name: no_dot_is_written_from_a_saved_record
test.purpose: A record carries the findings of a run rather than the topology they were drawn from, so regeneration warrants no companion even with an output path and the default in force.

test.name: graphml_is_off_unless_asked_for
test.purpose: With an output path but no request, no export is warranted: the export is opt-in, unlike the .dot companion.

test.name: graphml_needs_an_output_path
test.purpose: With the export requested but the report going to standard output, nothing is warranted — there is no path to derive the companion's name from.

test.name: graphml_is_written_when_asked_for_and_named
test.purpose: Both conditions together warrant the export.

test.name: the_companion_replaces_the_extension
