test.purpose: Each delivered language appears in the dependency report, so a pin that is immutable is not thereby invisible when it falls behind.

test.name: check-prereqs survives an unreachable upstream
test.purpose: An unreachable upstream reports "unknown" rather than failing or hanging: the report is a diagnostic a person runs, not a gate.

test.name: every runtime data file the build does not produce is tracked
test.purpose: Every file under the runtime location that the build does not itself produce is tracked by the repository, so that a version-control ignore rule cannot silently exclude product data. `.gitignore` carries `*.map` for linker map files, which also matched the extension table: it worked locally, was absent from the clone CI made, and every parsing test then failed naming the missing file rather than the rule that hid it.

test.name: HLR-043: elc does not modify the tree it analyses
test.purpose: The analysed tree checksums identically before and after a run.

test.name: HLR-043: elc opens nothing for writing
test.purpose: No syscall capable of modifying a file — an open carrying a writing mode, a creat, an unlink, a truncate, or a rename — is observed for the whole run. This is direct evidence of read-only operation, where comparing checksums afterwards is only circumstantial.

test.name: HLR-076: each source file is opened exactly once
test.purpose: No source file is opened twice for the whole run, which is the observable form of the single-parse rule: a second open would mean some stage re-read it.

test.name: HLR-009: the grammar is loaded from the runtime location, not linked
test.purpose: No grammar appears among the binary's link-time dependencies, and the grammar file is opened during the run — language support is loaded at run time rather than compiled in.

test.name: HLR-043: elc runs against a read-only directory
test.purpose: A run succeeds against a directory with write permission removed.

test.name: every linked library the Makefile takes from the distribution is installed by CI
test.purpose: `PKGS_BUILD` says which libraries elc links and takes from the distribution rather than building from source, and the workflow installs them on the runner; nothing connected the two. Phase 20 added libdw to one and not the other, and every compiling job failed at once while `make test` stayed green locally, the developer machine having the package already. Scoped to `lib*-dev`, which is exactly the set of linked libraries — the rest of PKGS_BUILD is the toolchain the runner image supplies.

test.name: HLR-125: the local sanitizer gate is as strong as the pipeline's
test.purpose: The sanitizer options the local target sets and those the pipeline sets are the same, and both abort on error. Without aborting, a leak reported inside a forked test child never reaches the parent's exit status, so a leaking unit test passes locally and fails only in CI — which is how Phase 11 shipped two of them.

test.name: HLR-135: deciding a conditional region spawns no preprocessor
test.purpose: The half a reading of the source cannot establish: a run over conditionally compiled source with definitions supplied issues one execve, the kernel's own. No cpp, no compiler, no build system.

test.name: HLR-135: deciding a conditional region reads no other file
test.purpose: The other half: each fixture source is opened once and nothing else in the tree is read. An implementation resolving an include to decide a condition would show the header here.

test.name: HLR-141: filtering by an image spawns no toolchain utility
test.purpose: A filtered run issues one execve, the kernel's own. No nm, no objdump, no readelf, no compiler and no linker — the half of the no-toolchain claim that reading the source cannot establish.

test.name: HLR-141: the image is opened once and nothing beside it
test.purpose: The image is read for its symbol table alone: opened once, with no second image searched for and no debugging information fetched from elsewhere. An implementation shelling out to a toolchain would show that tool's own reads.

test.name: HLR-141: an image carrying debug information is still opened once
test.purpose: The same claim against the case that can break it. Reading debug line information is what a DWARF library offers to do *elsewhere*: given the chance it resolves a `.gnu_debuglink` or a build-id and opens a file under a separate-debug directory the user never named. elc uses the low-level interface, which reads the descriptor it is handed and nothing else — a distinction one API call deep, invisible in `ldd`, and observable only here.

test.name: the link line names the runtime the demangler lives in
test.purpose: libstdc++ was already loaded as a transitive dependency, which is not enough to reference a symbol in it: a current ld will not resolve an undefined symbol from an indirect DT_NEEDED. Nothing else in the suite would catch the flag's removal, since ldd would still show the library.

test.name: every library the Makefile builds from source is built by CI
test.purpose: The pipeline reaches the whole from-source list through one makefile target and names no individual library, which is the only form of the statement that cannot drift from the makefile.

test.name: LLR-MAIN-01: a usage error opens no file under the target
test.purpose: Observed rather than read off main, because the property is about ordering and ordering is only visible from outside: a version that discovered targets and then validated the command line would produce the identical diagnostic and the identical exit status. The target exists and holds a source file, so the run has something it could open and must not.

test.name: LLR-USG-08: no string literal in the usage summary reaches the C11 limit
test.purpose: ISO C11 guarantees a translation unit supports string literals of 4095 characters and no more, and the build treats a warning as a defect — so a summary that outgrew the guarantee would stop the build rather than degrade. It outgrew it as soon as the option list reached this size; this is what keeps the literals split as options are added.

test.name: LLR-THR-11: only the threshold catalogue attributes a band
test.purpose: The claim to carry no opinion is checkable only if a reviewer can read one table rather than audit every analysis for a constant. What is checked is the citation of a band's published source; a module naming a measure it merely presents — a heading giving Martin's Instability formula, say — is a different thing and a required one.

test.name: LLR-BLD-06: the graph library brings in no second XML library
test.purpose: What building igraph with GraphML support off is worth. Its reader and writer are unused — elc writes GraphML itself — and enabling them links libxml2, which the project has no other need for. Asserted against the link line rather than the cmake flag, because the flag is the mechanism and this is the property.

test.name: the fixture level is wired and elc is runnable
test.purpose: The fixture-conformance level is wired and green before the first real fixture is written.

test.name: every expected-value file has a fixture header beside it
test.purpose: Guards the convention that expected values are hand-counted, never generated from elc's own output.

test.name: HLR-125: a usage error frees the declarations parsed before it
test.purpose: The case LLR-MAIN-19 was written for. A --stratum is accepted and allocates a layer owning its name and patterns; the --stratum-order after it names a layer never declared, which is a usage error. Nothing else in the suite takes this path — every other usage-error test fails before allocating anything — so until this test the requirement rested on inspection.

test.name: HLR-125: a usage error after two declarations is leak-clean
test.purpose: Two layers and a partial order, which LLR-STR-05 rejects because a partial order determines no direction. Both layers and every pattern each copied out of argv are outstanding when the parse fails.

test.name: HLR-125: a usage error after a scope declaration is leak-clean
test.purpose: The scope declarations copy their name and patterns as the strata do and for the same reason, so they leak the same way if the usage-error path forgets them.

test.name: HLR-125: an invalid target exits leak-clean
test.purpose: Past cli_parse and into discovery, which validates every target before walking any. The options are fully populated and the registry is open by now, so this path releases more than a usage error does.

test.name: HLR-125: a target that is neither file nor directory exits leak-clean
test.purpose: A FIFO named as a target: the same teardown reached through a different rejection, so a path that released correctly for a missing file but not for an unusable one is still caught.

test.name: HLR-125: a rejected saved record exits leak-clean
test.purpose: xml_read_report builds part of a model and then rejects the input. LLR-XRD-06 requires the partially built model be released rather than rendered, and this is what shows it was.

test.name: HLR-125: a structurally foreign record exits leak-clean
test.purpose: Well-formed XML of the wrong shape. The parser gets further before rejecting, so more of the model exists to be released than the malformed case leaves.

test.name: HLR-125: an unusable image exits leak-clean
test.purpose: elfsyms_open fails after the registry is open and before discovery runs (LLR-MAIN-20), which is a teardown ordering no successful run exercises.

test.name: HLR-125: an image that is not an object file exits leak-clean
test.purpose: The same fatal exit reached by a different rejection inside elfsyms_open, where libelf has been given a file it can open and cannot use.

test.name: HLR-125: a fatal runtime-location failure exits leak-clean
test.purpose: registry_open fails before anything else is acquired — the earliest fatal exit there is, and the one most likely to release something it never took.

test.name: HLR-124: a complete run over a real target is free of memory errors
test.purpose: The success path, instrumented. make valgrind covers this ground across every fixture; repeating one here is what makes this file a record of the ordinary run as well as of the error paths, which a record of the error paths alone would not be.

test.name: LLR-BLD-09: the build provides a sanitized configuration
test.purpose: The configuration HLR-124 and HLR-125 are verified under must instrument for all three things they name — memory error, undefined behaviour, and leaks. A gate missing one reports the other two and reads as clean.

test.name: LLR-BLD-09: the sanitized configuration rebuilds rather than reusing objects
test.purpose: An instrumented run against objects compiled without instrumentation reports nothing and passes, which is the failure a sanitizer gate is least able to notice about itself. The target must clean first.

test.name: HLR-125: the purification pass releases every vector it allocated
test.purpose: A run reaching graph purification over a tree that takes both branches of the pass — one directory with call edges and one without — is free of memory errors and leaks under instrumentation. Four library vectors are allocated per run on a path with several early returns, and none of them is reached by the baseline case above.

test.name: HLR-125: a rejected manifest exits leak-clean
test.purpose: A manifest refused part way through reading it — statements already allocated and a JSON document still held — exits with the fatal status and no leak. A run ending in a file the user must correct exits as leak-clean as one that succeeds.

test.name: HLR-125: a run writing every companion releases them all
test.purpose: A run producing the manifest, both drawings, the GraphML export and the matrix at once, followed by a second run reading back the manifest the first wrote, is free of memory errors and leaks — the shortest path through every allocation this phase adds.

test.name: HLR-125: a cyclic recovery view releases the components it collected
test.purpose: The branch a layered tree never reaches: three graph-library vectors and a rendered string per strongly connected component, on a path with its own early returns.

test.name: LLR-BLD-23: no function in elc is at or over the complexity threshold
test.purpose: The self-quality check, as a catalogued test rather than as something a person remembers running. PR #45 brought the source under the threshold and six phases of feature work put 43 functions back over it with nothing saying so; the section is read from the report elc produces over its own `src/`, so the threshold asserted against is the one elc applies to everyone else.

test.name: LLR-BLD-23: no critical finding against elc comes from an unexpected band
test.purpose: The bands of HLR-185, HLR-186 and HLR-192 are applied to elc's own source like anyone else's, and three of them fire. What must never appear is a critical finding from a band not named in the test, which would be a measurement newly turned on the product without anybody deciding to.

test.name: LLR-BLD-23: elc's own maintainability debt does not grow
test.purpose: A ratchet rather than a clean bill of health: fifteen of elc's own functions score below the critical maintainability band. The figure is recorded debt and not a target, asserted so the debt cannot quietly grow — the same contract test/gap-baseline.txt holds for coverage. It moved from twelve to fifteen when diagnostics were centralised, and the three that crossed are the metric's artefact rather than the code's: `fprintf` is a library call the graph cannot resolve and `diag_printf` is one it can, so every diagnosing function gained a point of fan-out, and `diag_printf` itself scores 51 for being called by seventy-nine functions despite being ten lines of complexity two.

test.name: LLR-BLD-24: elc's own components hold no dependency cycle
test.purpose: A cycle is what elc reports at critical severity in anyone else's code, and it had one: analyze.c included report.h for a single derivation, closing a loop with the module that renders what analysis produces.

test.name: LLR-BLD-25: no call in elc resolves ambiguously
test.purpose: A precondition of the claim above rather than a tidiness check. elc resolves a call by name, so two file-local statics sharing one make every call to it point at whichever module was indexed first — an edge in the wrong place, in the graph the acyclicity is measured over.

test.name: LLR-BLD-14: elc parses every one of its own source files
test.purpose: The delivered grammar cannot follow every construct C admits, and the project's answer is to avoid those constructs rather than to accept a per-file failure in its own report.

test.name: LLR-BLD-14: no source file of elc is skipped for want of a module
test.purpose: The other half of the same claim: a file measured around damage and a file never measured at all are different failures, and neither is acceptable in the delivered source.

test.name: HLR-181: the self-analysis is the ordinary run, not a special mode
test.purpose: Nothing above passes an option that relaxes anything, and the absence of such an option is part of the claim: a tool that needed one to measure itself cleanly would have measured nothing.
